rows.name: Pentaho
rows.reason: Its commercial ETL offering is relevant, but vendor documentation marks ODBC unsupported; a supported ODBC route and compliance with the no-open-source requirement remain unverified.

rows.name: Microsoft SQL Server Integration Services (SSIS)
rows.reason: ODBC ETL/scheduling documented; non-open-source license unverified. Vendors/driver/OS/edition/version unspecified; confirm destination/driver compatibility, license and unattended credentials. Throughput/recovery untested.

rows.name: Microsoft SQL Server Integration Services (SSIS) with SQL Server Agent
rows.reason: SSIS/SQL Server Agent supports ODBC extraction, transformation/loading and unattended scheduling. Verify licensed production edition/support, driver compatibility/bitness and throughput; efficient array operations depend on driver capabilities.

rows.name: EasyMorph Desktop with the commercial Server/Hub runtime
rows.reason: EasyMorph Desktop/commercial Server-Hub supports 64-bit ODBC transformation/scheduling. In-memory processing requires large-data testing; export mode, memory and historical Server/current Hub scope need verification. Opened pages undated.

rows.name: DBeaver Enterprise
rows.reason: Enterprise documentation/EULA support transfer, scheduling and vendor support. Verify ODBC/destination/service-account/unattended host operation; volume/consolidation untested. Proprietary product licensing does not exclude open-source dependencies, which are not prohibited.

rows.name: Advanced ETL Processor Enterprise
rows.reason: Windows ETL supports unattended transfers/transformations with vendor support. Feature page postdates question; guessed ODBC URL failed. Exact source and proprietary license remain unconfirmed despite advertised edition/license.

rows.name: Astera Centerprise with Data Integrator Server
rows.reason: Centerprise offers ODBC consolidation and unattended scheduling. Verify commercial server edition, support and source driver: documentation covers older versions; blocking transformations require workload sizing.

rows.name: Apache NiFi upstream distribution
rows.reason: Upstream Apache NiFi is Apache-2.0 licensed, conflicting with the explicit open-source prohibition. Automation capabilities do not cure this; any separately proposed commercial product requires its own license assessment.

rows.name: IBM InfoSphere DataStage
rows.reason: ODBC reading, transformations, destination writes, arrays and rejected-row handling documented in 2010. Current product/driver support requires confirmation; HTML documentation returned 403; scheduling appears only in a search excerpt.

rows.name: Apache NiFi upstream distribution
rows.reason: The upstream Apache distribution is open-source and does not itself supply the required commercial vendor support agreement, despite relevant automated dataflow capabilities.

rows.name: Apache Parquet
rows.reason: Parquet is an open-source columnar file format, not a supported ETL application that connects through ODBC, transforms tables, loads databases, and schedules monthly execution.

rows.name: Pentaho
rows.reason: Retain Pentaho Data Integration Enterprise for verification: recurring jobs documented. Commercial configuration is not proven to violate the license prohibition; exact license and ODBC/table-copy setup remain unresolved.

rows.name: Apache Parquet
rows.reason: Parquet is a column-oriented file format, not an ETL replacement: it neither copies database tables nor executes transfers itself. Intermediate-format use requires a separately chosen complete system.

rows.name: Safe Software FME Form with FME Flow
rows.reason: FME Form/Flow supports ODBC transformations and recurring execution. Budget both components and confirm support; generic ODBC works on Windows/Linux, not macOS. Actual-driver throughput remains untested.
